title: 20 Stocks Just Got Crushed by AI… Here are the 5 I'm Buying
creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
summary: In '20 Stocks Just Got Crushed by AI… Here are the 5 I'm Buying' (published 27 Sep 2026), Joseph Hogue, CFA argues Meta's new Muse personal AI agent is the first real killer app for agentic AI — bringing agents to consumer spending — and maps the ~20 stocks it upends. He likes PayPal (bought back at ~$50 after the takeover-offer rejection cratered it; ~10x P/E vs 16x a year ago, stablecoin growth) and Shopify (Muse users find its merchants' products and check out via Shop Pay; the rails underneath if Muse becomes shopping's front door) as the 'winners to buy'. Expedia is a conditional rebound play: its Muse partnership could redirect bookings through Expedia at Booking's expense, and the stock trades at 16x earnings vs a 25x average — though he stays cautious on the whole travel-middleman group (TripAdvisor, Airbnb, Booking, -15% to -24% in a month). On the AI-build side he ranks four neo-clouds — Oracle, Nebius, CoreWeave, IREN — and takes another look only at Nebius (his pick): ~500% revenue growth, best debt-to-free-cash-flow (-1.8x), 9.8x growth-adjusted P/S — while flagging Oracle's force majeure on a 2.5GW New Mexico data center as 'the first crack in the entire AI boom'. He avoids brokerages (Schwab, Raymond James, LPL, Ameriprise), banks (BofA, JPMorgan) and insurers (Progressive, Allstate) — AI agents could replace advice fees and erode sticky deposit-sweep profits — plus subscription names exposed to AI-driven cancellations (Adobe, SiriusXM, Match, Peloton, Planet Fitness, crushed 15%). Meta itself he holds: great story but ~30% above its 5-year average valuation after the 30% three-week run. Other tickers discussed with no call: Nvidia, Broadcom, AMD, Marvell, Salesforce, ServiceNow, AppLovin, Amazon. Caption note: auto-captions garble 'CoreWeave' as 'Corvus', 'IREN' as 'Iron', and 'Marvell' as 'Marvel'; tickers here are corrected.
